svg.text: Figure 3. The six pre-registered hypotheses (Holm over six, one-sided) and the external replication on LIDC-IDRI
NLST dev (discovery; Sybil's model selection split)
H1 the z-fix moves the score
share of exams whose 6-year logit moves
H2 the z-fix lowers the score
H3 the z-fix changes the alarm
share of exams whose alarm changes
alarms lost 27, gained 7 of 759 exams: the z-fix loses more than it adds
H4 a kernel change alters the alarm in < 5%
share of sharp/soft kernel pairs whose
test and dev both had 9 of 500 pairs with a changed alarm
H6 shared axis 0 carries the drop
H7 jump at a stretch change (partly seen)
b: 1-year logit change per change of stretch,
partly seen before the freeze; 121 of the 134 changed pairs involve GE
Counts, test (dev): z-fix exams 759 (924), participants 342 (424) for H1-H3 and H6; kernel pairs 500 (500) for H4; consecutive yearly pairs 4,353 (4,837), changed 134 (215) for H7.
z-fix: the same images given to Sybil at their true slice spacing (from the slice positions) instead of at the slice thickness. Alarm: Sybil's 1-year risk at or above
the frozen dev cut tau90 = 0.018. Axis 0: one direction shared by Sybil's five members in its pooled layer (frozen name "z-geometry"; an exploratory dev experiment
with no outcome read showed that it reads whether a thick slab of Sybil's own padding is in its 200-slice box; Figure 4). H5 and H5' were moved to the secondary list before the test split was opened.
LIDC-IDRI: 197 scans with strongly overlapping slices (one per patient; GE 134, Philips 46, Siemens 17), no cancer outcome, the frozen NLST dev SD (0.93) and axis 0, Holm over its
three tests; a different population (clinical CT), so it is a marker of replication, not part of the confirmatory family. Intervals: 95% participant bootstrap.
